expectation: Nuclear stain in intestinal-type epithelial cells only (crypt/villus or gland epithelium, or intestinal metaplasia), often abundant where present; stroma, muscle and immune cells should be negative, so nuclei light up in epithelial rows and glands.
notes: CDX2 signal is not nuclear: nuclei show as dark holes in a yellow haze. The haze covers the stroma and the tiled muscle block about as strongly as the epithelium, and the brightest spots are blobs that don't line up with nuclei. I found no nuclear-positive epithelial population.
observed: A: yellow haze across all tissue, including the muscle block on the right with tile seams. B: diffuse haze with blobs. C: the gland's nuclei are unstained and signal sits around them. D: blobs off the nuclei. E1: a cytoplasmic or texture pattern with dark nuclei, so it doesn't match nuclear CDX2.
why: The signal stays out of the nuclei and follows the tissue outline, the tiling and debris, not a nuclear-positive epithelial subset.
